more_info.overview: Colophony, also called rosin, is a resin material obtained from pine and related plants. This historical entry refers to esters of its resin acids rather than to unmodified rosin alone. Ester identity depends on the alcohol component used in the preparation. The broad group is listed here as a glazing material, while current food examples for a specific ester were not confirmed. It cannot be equated automatically with the separately specified glycerol esters of wood rosin.
more_info.uses: FDA lists particular glycerol and pentaerythritol esters of specified gum, wood or tall-oil rosins as plasticising materials in chewing-gum base. This does not identify a permission for every ester covered by the broad legacy name.
more_info.banned_in:
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
EU and US food-additive permissions for this exact entry were not confirmed in the sources checked in 2026.
